concepts.why: Biblical-theological / secular: Hag 2:5 says 'My Spirit remains among you', not 'dwell'; the name says more than this passage. Move it to concept 3 (with 'I am with you' in Hag 2:4) or drop.

Secular scholar, Jewish readers, Baptist/free church and Reformed alike: John 1:51 says nothing of a house of God or a gate of heaven; it shares only 'ascending and descending'. Set under this name it reads as the Gospel being Bethel's fulfilment, which no concept may say. Move it to a secondary line labelled only by the shared words (Gen 28:12 / John 1:51: 'ascending and descending'), or drop.

Secular scholar / Jewish reader: 2 Pet 1:18 says 'the holy mountain' (the Transfiguration setting); it does not say the place where you stand is holy, and set beside Sinai and the burning bush it shares only a word. It already appears under the cloud line in secondary concepts. Drop here.

note_fixes: Acts 7:44: the note quotes only the first sentence, which does not hold the concept; quote the part that does: 'It was constructed exactly as God had directed Moses, according to the pattern he had seen.'
concepts.why: Secular / Catholic / Orthodox: the passage is right (Heb 8:5 itself says 'a copy and shadow of what is in heaven', which is the text's own statement and may stand), but the Acts 7:44 note does not show the pattern. Optional addition from the same theme: 1 Chronicles 28:11-12, 19 (David given the plans for the temple 'in writing').

Secular scholar: Heb 9:5 says the cherubim overshadow the mercy seat; it does not say the LORD is enthroned, so it shares only 'cherubim'. It stands in the secondary line on the ark and mercy seat already. Drop here.

concepts.name: My house will be called a house of prayer
concepts.why: Jewish / secular / Baptist: the name 'for all the nations' is said only by Isa 56:7 and Mark 11:17 (and implied by 1 Kgs 8:42-43); 1 Kgs 8:30, 2 Chr 7:15, Matt 21:13 and Luke 1:10 speak of prayer at the house without the nations, so the name says more than most of its passages. The shorter name (Isa 56:7, Matt 21:13, Mark 11:17 all say it) holds every passage; the nations still show in Isa 56:7, Mark 11:17 and 1 Kgs 8:42-43.

concepts.name: The Word became flesh and made His dwelling among us
note_fixes: Matthew 1:23: the note splices with an ellipsis; use the exact words: 'they will call Him Immanuel' (which means, 'God with us').
concepts.why: Secular scholar and Jewish readers (and any reader of the text): only Matt 1:23 says 'God with us'. Matt 18:20 and 28:20 say 'I am with them / with you' in Jesus' mouth, and John 14:23 is the Father and Son making a home with a believer; none says what the name says, and gathered under it they read as the site asserting the identification. John 1:14 and Col 1:19, 2:9 do say 'dwelling / dwell' of Christ and take the dwelling language; Matt 1:23 keeps its own words. Move Matt 18:20, 28:20 to a new 'I am with you always' line (see missing) and John 14:23 to concept 35. The earlier name 'God with us' is acceptable if the drop is not made, but then the three 'I am with you' texts must go.

concepts.name: Destroy this temple, and in three days I will raise it up again
concepts.why: Secular scholar / Jewish readers / Reformed / Baptist: the name 'The temple of His body' is John's own explanation (2:21). Under it Matt 26:61, Mark 14:58 and Mark 15:29 (words of false witnesses and mockers, called false in Mark 14:56-57) read as the Synoptics agreeing that the saying means His body, which they do not say. Naming the concept by the saying itself (John 2:19) holds all five saying-passages and leaves John 2:21 as the gospel's own comment. Matt 12:6 ('One greater than the temple is here') does not contain the saying; give it its own line (see missing) or drop it.

All readers: Rev 3:12 says the overcomer will be a pillar IN the temple of My God, not that believers are the temple; it shares the word 'temple'. Move it to 'The LORD is in His holy temple' (concept 24) or drop. John 14:23 ('make Our home with him') may be added here from concept 33, as 'home' with a believer is nearer 'you are God's temple' than 'God with us'.

Baptist / dispensational and Reformed readers part on whether Isa 60 speaks of Israel's restored Zion or of the new Jerusalem; set under a Revelation name it reads as Isaiah 60 being Revelation 21's city, the Israel-and-the-church question. Isa 60:19 also says nothing of a temple. Drop (or leave as one line in secondary concepts under 'light' with a neutral shared-word label). Rev 21:2, 21:23, 22:1-2 and 22:5 do not say 'no temple' either but are the city around the verse that does; acceptable as the passage's own setting.

concepts.name: My dwelling place will be with them
concepts.why: Baptist / dispensational and Reformed / Catholic: 'The dwelling place of God is with man' is Rev 21:3 alone; Ezek 37:26-27, 43:7 and 48:35 speak of the Israelites and a city, and gathered under a Revelation name they read as one being the other, the Israel-and-the-church question. Ezek 37:27 'My dwelling place will be with them' is the text both Ezekiel and Rev 21:3 use, and the new name is in the texts' words without choosing. The closing rule holds: this is the theme's own hope, from passages within the theme, and the dark is left standing in 31 and 32. Hag 2:9 does not say 'dwelling'; keep it only as 'the latter glory of this house', which it is.

secondary_or_links: Order of the concepts: 32 ('The glory has departed') immediately followed by 33 ('God with us') reads as answer-and-fulfilment. The order is the canon's, and no name asserts it, so it may stand; but no connecting words ('therefore', 'answer') should be added, and nothing in 33-36 may be named so that it replaces what 18-32 describe.
Add a neutral secondary line for the ladder: 'Ascending and descending' - Genesis 28:12 and John 1:51 (shared words only), in place of John 1:51 under concept 6.
Secondary 'Worship -> in spirit and in truth' (John 4:21-23) is acceptable because the verse is quoted in full with 'salvation is from the Jews'; keep the full verse, not an excerpt.
Secondary 'The cloud -> a voice from the cloud' (Exod 24:16, Matt 17:5, 2 Pet 1:17-18) is fine: the grouping is the shared voice from the cloud, and the Transfiguration is not called Sinai.

Links: 'Judgment' and 'Sin/Exile/Death' are rightly kept; consider adding 'Israel' / 'Land' if the site has such themes (the theme runs through Zion, the Name and the city), and 'Water' / river if one exists (see missing).

missing.sub_theme: Not one stone will be left on another
missing.why: Every reader of the temple theme expects the destruction foretold in the Gospels beside 1 Kgs 9:7-8 and Jer 26:6; the outline has the exile of the first temple (31, 32) but nothing on the second. Name it in the texts' own words, without dating or interpretation.

missing.sub_theme: Water flowing from beneath the threshold of the temple
missing.why: The river from the house, with the trees whose leaves do not wither, is the single largest Ezekiel 40-48 passage not in the outline; it is the text behind Rev 22:1-2 in concept 36 and the river of Gen 2:10 in concept 5, and a reader of the theme would look for it.

missing.sub_theme: Who is left among you who saw this house in its former glory?
missing.why: The rebuilding of the house after the exile and the grief and joy at its laying are the plain link between 'The glory has departed' and Hag 2:9 in the closing concept; without it the outline passes from the destruction of Jerusalem to Haggai with no account of the second house.

Matt 28:20 and 18:20 move out of concept 33 (see there); a reader of this theme expects the promise of presence at the end of Matthew somewhere in it. As a line in its own right it makes no claim beyond the words 'I am with you'.

missing.sub_theme: One greater than the temple is here
missing.why: Matt 12:6 leaves concept 34; as its own line it states what is said and no more. Only needed if it is not kept in secondary concepts.
